question.problem: A nonzero vector $⟨a,\,0,\,c⟩$ is parallel to the plane $r\cdot ⟨-1,1,3⟩=\sqrt{7}.$ What is the value of $\frac{a}{c}?$
question.worked_solution:
We need a vector $v=⟨{t}_{1},{t}_{2},{t}_{3}⟩$ that is parallel to the given plane. 

From the equation $r\cdot ⟨-1,1,3⟩=\sqrt{7}$ of the plane, we get the normal vector $n=⟨-1,1,3⟩.$ So, $v⊥n$ and we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}v\cdot n & =0 \\ ⟨{t}_{1},{t}_{2},{t}_{3}⟩\cdot ⟨-1,1,3⟩ & =0 \\ -{t}_{1}+{t}_{2}+3{t}_{3} & =0 \\ {t}_{1} & ={t}_{2}+3{t}_{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we obtain 

$$
v=⟨{t}_{2}+3{t}_{3},\,{t}_{2},{t}_{3}⟩,
$$

where ${t}_{2},{t}_{3}\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ 

We are told that the second component of $v$ equals $0.$ So, we must set ${t}_{2}=0.$ 

Since $v$ is nonzero, we can pick any ${t}_{3}\ne 0.$ For example, setting ${t}_{3}=1$, we get

$$
v=⟨3,\,0,\,1⟩.
$$

Therefore, $\frac{a}{c}=3.$
